On this question of maintainability of a revision petition U/s 397 Cr.P.C before Sessions Court against an order of Magistrate U/s 156(3) Cr.P.C directing the police to register an FIR and investigate the same, this Court is guided by the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court titled as Nishu Wadhwa Vs. Siddharth Wadhwa 2017 Online Del 6444 in which after considering the judgment of Father Thomas (Supra), it was held as under:-
"13.

sentences.text: The issue that since the accused has not been summoned as an accused and has no right to file a revision petition is allen, while deciding an application under Section 156 (3) Cr.P.C.
The said issue crops up when the Magistrate entertains the complaint and on taking cognizance proceeds as a complaint case.
In case directions are issued for registration of FIR immediately, on registration of FIR, the person against whom allegations are made in the FIR attains the status of an accused.
His rights in so far as the Police can summon him for investigation, arrest him without warrants for allegations of cognizable offences are duly affected.

In a situation where the fundamental right of freedom and liberty of a person is affected, it cannot be held that he has no right to Digitally signed by SUNIL SUNIL GUPTA GUPTA Date:
2023.01.21 17:47:54 +0530 be heard at that stage.

Thus to hold that since directions only have been issued under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C, and no cognizable has been taken thus no revision would lie would be an erroneous reading of the decisions of the Supreme Court.
Therefore, an order dismissing or allowing an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C is not an interlocutor order and a revision petition against the same is maintainable."
9. Considering the above, it appears that the law is settled on this particular aspect as this Court is bound by the law laid down by Hon'ble Delhi High Court.
So, it is held that present revision petition is maintainable in law.

The offences mentioned therein are related to sexual offences against woman.
The respondent has alleged the commission of offences U/s 323/354/354B/452/506/509 IPC in her complaint U/s 200 Cr.P.C as well as the application U/s 156 (3) Cr.P.C.

As section 354 and Section 354B IPC have been specifically mentioned in the explanation to Section 197 (1) Cr.P.C,
so it appears that there was no requirement of obtaining a previous sanction by the respondent herein.

Another ground taken by Ld. Counsel for revisionists is that the impugned order is bad in law due to the bar as contained in Section 140, Delhi Police Act 1978.

It was argued that the complaint U/s 200 Cr.P.C alongwith the application U/s 153 (3) Cr.P.C was filed before Ld. Magistrate on 01.02.2020 i.e., more than four months after the alleged incident hence, same was liable to be dismissed in the absence of previous sanction of the Administrator as per Section 140, Delhi Police Act.
Ld. Counsel for respondent on the other hand has argued that the alleged offence cannot be said as having being done by the revisionists under colour of duty by any stretch of imagination.
So, it was argued that reliance on Section 140 Delhi Police Act is misconceived as same has no application in these facts.

13. Section 140 Delhi Police Act provides as under:-
"140.

(i) In case of alleged offence by a police officer or other person, or of a wrong alleged to have been done by such police officer or other person, by any act done under colour of duty or authority or in excess of an such duty or authority, or wherein it shall appear to the Court that the offence of wrong if committed or done was of the character aforesaid, the prosecution or suit shall not be entertained and if entertained shall be dismissed if it is instituted, more than three months after the date of the act complained of:
Provided that any such prosecution against a Police Officer of other person may be entertained by the Court, if instituted with the previous sanction of the Administrator, within one year from the date of the offence.
(ii) In case of an intended suit on account of such Digitally signed by SUNIL SUNIL GUPTA GUPTA Date:

Said provision reveals that the bar applies only to alleged offences done under colour of duty.
Now the question is whether the allegations leveled by respondent herein will be covered under the expression "colour of duty".
To find answer to this question, it will be relevant to refer the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Paul George Vs. State of NCT of Delhi Crl. Appeal No. 501/2008.

sentences.text: In that case, the petitioner/appellant before the Court was working as a Head Constable with Delhi Police at the time of alleged incident.
He was directed to go to the Police Headquarters at ITO to convey an urgent message thereupon he left the PS driving a police Mini Truck No. DDL-6462.
While the vehicle reached under railway bridge on Ring Road going to Jamuna Bazar, it went over the road divider and hit a Scooter which resulted in the death of the pillion rider.
He was convicted after trial by Ld. Magistrate for the offences u/s 279/304A IPC.
The conviction and sentence was confirmed by first appellate Court and High Court.

It was argued before Hon'ble Supreme Court that the prosecution against the Digitally signed by SUNIL SUNIL GUPTA GUPTA Date:
2023.01.21 17:49:02 +0530 appellant was barred U/s 140 (1) of Delhi Police Act as same was not initiated within three months of the incident.

Hon'ble Supreme Court interpreted the expression "colour of duty" in this factual background as under:-
"8.
It is therefore evident that what has to be seen on the facts of the case is the nature of the act and as to whether it felt within the protection available to the appellant.

The facts of the present case shows that the appellant, a Head Constable Driver, was posted at Kashmere Gate Police Station had been entrusted with the task of delivering a wireless message to the Police Head Quarters at the ITO in New Delhi and while on his way he had suddenly gone over the road divider which separated the lanes and had hit the scooter which was oncoming in the opposite lane.

It is this act,
the appellant had caused the death of one person and injuries to the other.

Undoubtedly the duty entrusted to the appellant to deliver the message to the Police Head Quarters was in his capacity as a police officer and to that extent and prima facie he would be protected by Section 140 of the Act.
We find however, that by jumping road divider and coming-face on the incoming traffic was the factor which had caused the accident and was clearly not a matter within the colour of duty.

We are, therefore, of the opinion that the case of the appellant would not be covered by Section 140 and that the initiation of proceedings and the prosecution beyond three months from the date of accident was not beyond limitation."

18. On this aspect, it will be relevant to quote the observations of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Lalita Kumari Vs. State of U.P & Ors. Write Petition Crl. No. 68/2008 to the following effect:-

sentences.text:
"67. It has to be noted that in Section 154(1) of the Code, the legislature in its collective wisdom Digitally signed by SUNIL SUNIL GUPTA GUPTA Date:
2023.01.21 17:49:30 +0530 has carefully and cautiously used the expression "information" without qualifying the same as in Sections 41(1)(a) or (g) of the Code wherein the expressions "reasonable complaint" and "credible information" are used.

Evidently, the non- qualification of the word "information" in Section 154(1) unlike in Sections 41(1)(a) and (g) of the Code may be for the reason that the police officer should not refuse to record an information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence and to register a case thereon on the ground that he is not satisfied with the reasonableness or credibility of the information.

In other words, "reasonableness"
or "credibility" of the said information is not a condition precedent for registration of a case.

A comparison of the present Section 154 with those of the earlier Codes will indicate that the legislature had purposely thought it fit to employ only the word "information" without qualifying the said word.

Section 139 of the Code of Criminal Procedure of 1861 (Act 25 of 1861) passed by the Legislative Council of India read that "every complaint or information" preferred to an officer in charge of a police station should be reduced into writing which provision was subsequently modified Asi Paramjeet vs Smt. Meenu on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199696570/
9 by Section 112 of the Code of 1872 (Act 10 of 1872) which thereafter read that "every complaint"
preferred to an officer in charge of a police station shall be reduced in writing.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The word "complaint"
which occurred in previous two Codes of 1861 and 1872 was deleted and in that place the word "information" was used in the Codes of 1882 and 1898

which word is now used in Sections 154, 155,
157 and 190(c) of the Code.

An overall reading of all the Codes makes it clear that the condition which is sine qua non for recording a first information report is that there must be an information and that information must Digitally signed by SUNIL SUNIL GUPTA GUPTA Date:
2023.01.21 17:49:42 +0530 disclose a cognizable offence."
19. Ld. CMM vide impugned order dated 17.03.2020 has merely directed the police to register an FIR on the basis of allegations made by respondent in the complaint filed there.
By issuing such a direction, Ld. Court has not accepted the allegations therein as true.
Moreover, it is not necessary that the allegations have to be true for registration of FIR.

Only requirement is that the information/
allegations should disclose cognizable offence.
The respondent whose several relatives are allegedly involved in commission of various offences, is also entitled to protection of law.
Her allegations of sexual assault cannot be simply brushed aside on that count alone without investigation.
Whether the alleged incident took place or not, is subject matter of investigation.
In case, the allegations are found to be false after investigation as per law, the revisionists would be entitled to avail legal remedies available to them.

Further observations of Hon'ble Apex Court in Lalita Kumari (Supra) on this aspect are being reproduced below:-
"100)
The registration of FIR under Section 154 of the Code and arrest of an accused person under Section 41 are two entirely different things.
It is not correct to say that just because FIR is registered, the accused person can be arrested immediately.

It is the imaginary fear that "merely because FIR has been registered, it would require arrest of the accused and thereby leading to loss of his reputation" and it should not be allowed by this Court to hold that registration of FIR is not mandatory to avoid such inconvenience to some persons.

The remedy lies in strictly enforcing the safeguards available against arbitrary arrests made Digitally signed by SUNIL SUNIL GUPTA GUPTA Date:
2023.01.21 17:49:56 +0530 by the police and not in allowing the police to avoid mandatory registration of FIR when the information discloses commission of a cognizable offence.
XXXXX 102)
Besides, the Code gives power to the police to close a matter both before and after investigation.
A police officer can foreclose an FIR before an investigation under Section 157 of the Code, if it appears to him that there is no sufficient ground to investigate the same.
The Section itself states that a police officer can start investigation when he has a 'reason to suspect the commission of an offence'.

Therefore, the requirements of launching an investigation under Section 157 of the Asi Paramjeet vs Smt. Meenu on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199696570/
10 Code are higher than the requirement under Section 154 of the Code.
The police officer can also, in a given case, investigate the matter and then file a final report under Section 173 of the Code seeking closure of the matter.
Therefore, the police is not liable to launch an investigation in every FIR which is mandatorily registered on receiving information relating to commission of a cognizable offence."

20. Considering the above discussion, this Court is of the view that Ld. CMM has rightly directed SHO, PS Ambedkar Nagar to register an FIR as the allegations prima facie disclose commission of a cognizable offence.
Accordingly, no ground is made out to interfere with the said order under revisional jurisdiction of this Court.
Needless to say that the observations made in this order shall not influence/ affect the investigation in any manner and same shall be done as per law.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The explanation attached to Section 197 (1) Cr.P.C mentioned above clearly states that no sanction as mentioned in Sub-Section(1) shall be required in case of a public servant accused of offences mentioned therein.
The offences mentioned therein are related to sexual offences against woman.
The respondent has alleged the commission of offences U/s 323/354/354B/452/506/509 IPC in her complaint U/s 200 Cr.P.C as well as the application U/s 156 (3) Cr.P.C.
It is this act,
the appellant had caused the death of one person and injuries to the other.
Undoubtedly the duty entrusted to the appellant to deliver the message to the Police Head Quarters was in his capacity as a police officer and to that extent and prima facie he would be protected by Section 140 of the Act.
We find however, that by jumping road divider and coming-face on the incoming traffic was the factor which had caused the accident and was clearly not a matter within the colour of duty.
So, the protection of Section 140 Delhi Police Act will not be available to the revisionists in present matter.
19. Ld. CMM vide impugned order dated 17.03.2020 has merely directed the police to register an FIR on the basis of allegations made by respondent in the complaint filed there.
By issuing such a direction, Ld. Court has not accepted the allegations therein as true.
Moreover, it is not necessary that the allegations have to be true for registration of FIR.
Only requirement is that the information/
allegations should disclose cognizable offence.
The respondent whose several relatives are allegedly involved in commission of various offences, is also entitled to protection of law.
Her allegations of sexual assault cannot be simply brushed aside on that count alone without investigation.
Whether the alleged incident took place or not, is subject matter of investigation.
In case, the allegations are found to be false after investigation as per law, the revisionists would be entitled to avail legal remedies available to them.
It is the imaginary fear that "merely because FIR has been registered, it would require arrest of the accused and thereby leading to loss of his reputation" and it should not be allowed by this Court to hold that registration of FIR is not mandatory to avoid such inconvenience to some persons.
The remedy lies in strictly enforcing the safeguards available against arbitrary arrests made Digitally signed by SUNIL SUNIL GUPTA GUPTA Date:
2023.01.21 17:49:56 +0530 by the police and not in allowing the police to avoid mandatory registration of FIR when the information discloses commission of a cognizable offence.
